title: 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼  (Guard Your Own Rice Bowl)

segments.t: Right after telling the rookies never to cave to backstage favours, Tak Ye-jin gets Ra Joon-mo's call on speakerphone in front of both teams. Listen for the word for 'a favour' and the expression for 'rice bowl' — meaning your own livelihood and turf.
우리 라준모 피디가 나한테 무슨 부탁이 있는데?
그쪽에서 사전 녹화 좀 떠주면 안 되냐?
안 돼, 그날은 무대가 많아요.
아 좀, 뮤뱅 피디님, 부탁 좀 합시다!
우리 각자도생합시다.
이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
돼요, 안 돼요?
얘가 분위기 파악 못 하네.
Let's savour the eight lines of Joon-mo's speakerphone humiliation.
우리 라준모 피디가 나한테 무슨 부탁이 있는데?

'What favour does our PD Ra Joon-mo have to ask me?' Showing off in front of the rookies, Ye-jin puts 'our' teasingly before Joon-mo's name, then pairs the word for a favour or personal request with 'to me' This means that.
그쪽에서 사전 녹화 좀 떠주면 안 되냐?

'Couldn't your side pre-record them for us?' He points politely to 'your team over there' and refers to taping a performance ahead of the live show, ending with a casual Korean phrasing for 'couldn't you please...?' It is a handy word.
안 돼, 그날은 무대가 많아요.

'No way, we have lots of stages that day.' First comes a blunt 'no can do', then she switches to a polite 'there are many' because she knows his writers are listening, mentioning the stage performances We built from this.
아 좀, 뮤뱅 피디님, 부탁 좀 합시다!
'Come on, Music Bank PD, let me ask this one favour!' Swallowing his pride, Joon-mo tacks an honorific suffix onto 'PD' and pleads, 'let's please make this request happen' This short for that.
우리 각자도생합시다.
'Let's each fend for ourselves.' Ye-jin drops a punchy four-syllable idiom meaning 'everyone survives on their own', turning it into a brisk 'let's each handle our own show!' It comes from this.
이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.

'In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.' Hanging up, she lectures the rookies using slang that literally means 'this floor' for 'this industry', then compares your job and turf to a 'rice bowl' that you have to take care of yourself This short for that.
돼요, 안 돼요?

'Is it on, or is it off?' Back in Joon-mo's room, Ji-yeon cuts straight to the chase with a four-syllable phrase literally meaning 'does it work, doesn't it work?' — the quickest way to settle any yes-or-no decision in Korean We built from this.
얘가 분위기 파악 못 하네.

'She really can't read the room.' Embarrassed in front of his staff, Joon-mo mutters Korean's exact match for 'reading the room', combining the words for mood or atmosphere and grasping it is a handy word. Now let's listen to the whole speakerphone showdown again.
우리 라준모 피디가 나한테 무슨 부탁이 있는데?
그쪽에서 사전 녹화 좀 떠주면 안 되냐?
안 돼, 그날은 무대가 많아요.
아 좀, 뮤뱅 피디님, 부탁 좀 합시다!
우리 각자도생합시다.
이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
돼요, 안 돼요?
얘가 분위기 파악 못 하네.
You now have the expressions for asking a favour, demanding a quick yes-or-no, and reading the room. Next, Director Jang calls Joon-mo in!
안녕히 가세요!
